A **randomized test** is a randomized procedure with binary action space
whose action set is $\{0,1\}$, equipped with its full sigma-algebra
$2^{\{0,1\}}$ (the power set, which is a sigma-algebra by
[[def-sigma-algebra]]), where $1$ means reject and $0$ means do not reject
([[def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel]]). Its **test function** is
$$\varphi(x)=K(x,\{1\}),\qquad x\in\mathcal X.$$
Since $K(x,\cdot)$ is a probability measure and $\{0\},\{1\}$ partition the
action set, $K(x,\{0\})+K(x,\{1\})=1$. Thus $\varphi(x)\in[0,1]$ and
$1-\varphi(x)=K(x,\{0\})$ is the probability of not rejecting. Give $[0,1]$
the trace of the Borel sigma-algebra on $[0,+\infty]$, namely
$\{C\cap[0,1]:C\in\mathcal B([0,+\infty])\}$. By
[[lem-procedure-action-law-is-measurable]], $x\mapsto K(x,\{1\})$ is
measurable; since it has range in $[0,1]$, its preimage of $C\cap[0,1]$ equals
its preimage of $C$ and is measurable for every such $C$. Hence $\varphi$ is a
measurable map in the preimage sense of
[[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]]. Its value is the
rejection probability after observing $x$.

By [F4], the simple-null size is $E_0[\varphi(X)]$; [F10] identifies it with $P_0(X>L_C)$. Thus $L_C$ is an exact critical level by [F8].

For any $c\ge0$, the affine law in [F1] and CDF definition [F12] give $P_c(X\le L_C)=\Phi((L_C-c)/\sigma_0)$. By strict increase and uniqueness in [F2], this equals $\beta$ exactly when $(L_C-c)/\sigma_0=z_\beta$. Hence the unique solution is $c=\sigma_0(z_{1-\alpha}-z_\beta) =\sigma_0(z_{1-\alpha}+z_{1-\beta})$, using the symmetry in [F2]. Since $z_{1/2}=0$ and $\Phi$ is strictly increasing by [F2], while $1-\alpha,1-\beta>1/2$, both quantiles in the sum are positive. This solution is therefore the least positive concentration and is $L_D$ by [F8].

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume AC, $\sigma_0>0$, $0<\alpha,\beta<1/2$, and $k_Q>0$. Consider the
response-only experiment with concentration $c\in[0,\infty)$ and
$X\sim N(c,\sigma_0^2)$ under each $c$. Reject the blank when
$X>L_C$. For the coefficient-of-variation criterion
$\operatorname{CV}(c)\le k_Q$, the exact critical level, detection limit
for false-negative target $\beta$, and quantification limit are
$$L_C=z_{1-\alpha}\sigma_0,\qquad L_D=(z_{1-\alpha}+z_{1-\beta})\sigma_0,\qquad L_Q=\frac{\sigma_0}{k_Q}.$$
where $z_q$ is the unique standard normal $q$-quantile from
[[lem-standard-normal-cdf-quantiles-and-symmetry]]. These formulas are
conditional on the known-blank, equal-variance normal model.

$$z_{1-q}=-z_q.$$

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $Z$ have the standard normal law and let
$\Phi(x)=P(Z\le x)$ be its cumulative distribution function. Then $\Phi$ is
continuous and strictly increasing, with limits $0$ and $1$ at $-\infty$ and
$+\infty$, and $P(Z=x)=0$ for every $x\in\mathbb R$. For each $q\in(0,1)$
there is a unique real $z_q$ with
$\Phi(z_q)=q$, and
$$z_{1-q}=-z_q.$$

Assume AC. For $m\in\mathbb R$, $\sigma\ge0$, and a real random variable
$X$ with law $N(m,\sigma^2)$,
$$E[X]=m,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(X)=\sigma^2.$$

Assume AC. Define $\gamma(E)=\int_E e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}\,dx$ for Borel E in $\mathbb R$. By [[lem-normal-density-has-total-mass-one]] and [[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]], gamma is a probability measure; denote it $N(0,1)$. For $m\in\mathbb R$ and $\sigma\ge0$, define $N(m,\sigma^2)$ as the law of $x\mapsto m+\sigma x$ on $(\mathbb R,\mathcal B,\gamma)$. This affine map is continuous: for $\sigma$>0 choose $\delta$=$\varepsilon$/$\sigma$, and for $\sigma$=0 it is constant. Its inverse images of opens are open, so it is Borel measurable. [[lem-law-of-a-random-element-is-a-probability-measure]] makes its pushforward a probability. When $\sigma$=0, the preimage of E is all of R if m belongs to E and empty otherwise, so $N(m,0)=\delta_m$ in [[def-dirac-measure]].

Let $X$ be a real random variable. Its **cumulative distribution function** is
the function
$$F_X:\mathbb R\to[0,1],\qquad F_X(x):=\mathbb P(X\le x)=\mathbb P_X((-\infty,x]).$$

Let $C=[0,\infty)$ be a concentration parameter set and let
$$\mathsf E=((\mathbb R,\mathcal B(\mathbb R)),C,(P_c)_{c\in C})$$
be a statistical experiment ([[def-statistical-experiment]]). The response
$X(x)=x$ is a real random variable ([[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]])
with law $P_c$ at concentration $c$; $P_0$ is the blank law. Since each
$(t,\infty)$ is open, it is Borel ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]), so the
indicator rule below is measurable. For a
threshold $t\in\mathbb R$, the positive-decision rule is
$\varphi_t(x)=\mathbf 1_{\{x>t\}}$. Its blank false-positive probability is
$P_0(X>t)$, and its false-negative probability at $c>0$ is $P_c(X\le t)$.
These are the null rejection probability and one minus the power for the
simple null $\{0\}$ and point alternative $\{c\}$
([[def-randomized-test]], [[def-test-size-and-power]],
[[cor-expectation-of-an-indicator-is-probability]],
[[lem-probability-measure-basic-identities]]).

1. $\mathbb P(A^c)=1-\mathbb P(A)$.
2. If $A\subseteq B$, then $\mathbb P(A)\le\mathbb P(B)$.
3. If $A\subseteq B$, then $\mathbb P(B\setminus A)=\mathbb P(B)-\mathbb P(A)$.
4. $\mathbb P(\bigcup_n A_n)\le\sum_{n=0}^\infty \mathbb P(A_n)$, and for every
   natural $m$,
   $$\mathbb P\left(\bigcup_{n<m}A_n\right)\le\sum_{n<m}\mathbb P(A_n).$$
5. $\mathbb P(A\cup B)=\mathbb P(A)+\mathbb P(B)-\mathbb P(A\cap B)$.
6. If $A_n\uparrow A$, then
   $$\mathbb P(A)=\sup_n\mathbb P(A_n).$$
   If $A_n\downarrow A$, then
   $$\mathbb P(A)=\inf_n\mathbb P(A_n).$$

routine_steps.claim: At $c=0$, the model is $N(0,\sigma_0^2)$, so [F3] represents $Y_0=\sigma_0Z$ in law. Set $L_C=z_{1-\alpha}\sigma_0$; by [F1], [F3], and complement identity [F6], $P_0(Y_0>L_C)=1-\Phi(z_{1-\alpha})=\alpha$. Also [F1] gives $z_{1/2}=-z_{1/2}$, hence $z_{1/2}=0$ and $\Phi(0)=1/2$. Since $1-\alpha>1/2$, strict increase gives $z_{1-\alpha}>0$, and [F5] makes this an exact critical level.

By [F2], $\operatorname{CV}(c)=\sigma(c)/c =\sigma_0/c+\rho\sigma_0$ for $c>0$. If $k_Q>\rho\sigma_0$, the inequality $\operatorname{CV}(c)\le k_Q$ is equivalent to $c\ge\sigma_0/(k_Q-\rho\sigma_0)$, giving the displayed least value. If $k_Q\le\rho\sigma_0$, then $\operatorname{CV}(c)>\rho\sigma_0\ge k_Q$ for every finite $c>0$, so no finite quantification limit exists.

For $c>0$, the scale is $\sigma(c)=\sigma_0(1+\rho c)>0$. By [F3], $P_c(Y\le L_C)=\Phi((L_C-c)/\sigma(c))$. Since $a=z_{1-\beta}>0$, strict increase in [F1] makes this equal to $\beta$ exactly when $c-L_C=a\sigma_0(1+\rho c),\qquad a=z_{1-\beta}>0.$ Rearranging gives $c(1-a\rho\sigma_0)=L_C+a\sigma_0$, whose right-hand side is positive. If $a\rho\sigma_0<1$, the unique solution is the positive displayed $L_D$. If $a\rho\sigma_0=1$, the equation would equate zero to a positive number; if $a\rho\sigma_0>1$, its only algebraic solution is negative. Thus a nonnegative detection limit exists exactly under the stated condition.

If the recorded observation is the category $Y\le L_C$, its probability under the stated law is the CDF at $L_C$, namely the displayed $\Phi((L_C-c)/\sigma(c))$ by [F4]. The affine normal law has no atom at $L_C$ by [F1] and [F3], while the CDF gives the probability of the reported half-line. Substituting $L_C$ as an observed point is therefore not the likelihood of this censored report.
